clue.text: Criticise cuts removing last source of economies

indicators.note: tells us to drop the final letter of the word for cuts

parts.note: snips are small cuts, as with scissors

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone complains about spending cuts that no longer bring any savings.
explanation.definitionFit: To snipe is to make sly, carping attacks, a form of criticism.

clue.text: Writer succeeded with two newspapers

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
the i and the FT (Financial Times) are two British newspapers, giving I and FT

explanation.surface: An author makes it big writing for a pair of papers.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a British national daily and the FT is the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift was the Irish satirist who wrote Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Current pair involved in deal unlikely to invest

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
in bridge, North and South are a partnership taking part in each deal
tall, as in a tall story, means hard to believe

explanation.surface: Two people in a business deal are reluctant to put money in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invest' looks financial, but here it means to place someone formally in office; 'deal' is the dealing of cards in bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest someone with an office is to induct them into it formally, as a bishop is.

clue.text: Artists say love isn't represented in lives

parts.note: to say something is to express it

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed inside the word for lives

parts.note: lives as a verb: he lives, he is
love is zero in tennis, written as O

indicators.note: re-presented, laid out again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Painters claim that affection is absent from their lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges ISNT into NIST; with O (love) it goes 'in' IS. 'lives' is the verb, not the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Expressionism was an early twentieth-century art movement whose painters, such as Munch, are its members.

clue.text: Boast about argument

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone brags about winning a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow over something is to gloat or brag about it.

clue.text: Assistant on course to stop working under disreputable man

indicators.note: in a down clue the second part sits below the first

parts.note: a cad is an ungentlemanly scoundrel
a machine dies when it stops working

explanation.surface: A helper on a course quits, being employed by a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A caddie carries a golfer's clubs and gives advice on the golf course.

clue.text: Coroner beginning to doubt suspect is publicly known

indicators.note: used as an adjective: dubious, out of true, so the letters are disordered
the start of the word doubt gives its first letter

explanation.surface: A coroner begins to have doubts that a suspect's identity is common knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on record has been officially stated and so is available for anyone to know.

clue.text: Person who invents revolutionary form of transport

indicators.note: something revolving turns round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a liar invents stories

explanation.surface: An inventor comes up with a radical new means of getting about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person who invents' suggests an engineer, but the invention here is lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Rail means railways, a mode of travel, as in going by rail.

clue.text: Judge's rare outburst interrupted by boring part

definitions.note: read as judge is, the noun before the link

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are broken into by the inserted word
a burst of letters flying out of order signals the rearrangement

parts.note: a drill bit is the part of a drill that bores

explanation.surface: A judge, normally restrained, erupts at a dull passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outburst' rearranges RARE into ARER for the drill BIT to split. 'boring part' looks like a tedious section of a trial, but a drill bit is what bores.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is someone appointed to settle disputes, a referee or adjudicator.

clue.text: Play in which King Lear goes mad and loses throne ultimately

indicators.note: Lear's madness signals a scramble of the letters

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: tells us a letter is dropped from the name Lear
the final letter of the word throne is the one meant

explanation.surface: A drama in which the old king loses his mind and his crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' drops E, the last of throne, from LEAR to leave LAR; with K, 'goes mad' rearranges KLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To lark about is to fool around or play mischievously.

clue.text: Scholar up to no good with writer worried about being confined

indicators.note: up to no good suggests mischief, the letters being messed about

parts.note: a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: An academic misbehaves alongside an author who fears enclosed spaces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no good' rearranges SCHOLAR UPTO into CLAUSTROPHO; 'writer' is a pen, not an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Claustrophobia is the fear of being shut in small spaces.

clue.text: Popular drink imbibed on vacation is tasteless

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a sip is a small drink

indicators.note: the word imbibed is emptied of its middle, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A trendy beverage drunk on holiday turns out to be bland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbibed' looks like a verb for the drink, but 'on vacation' empties it to ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid food or drink lacks flavour; it is bland.

clue.text: Safety feature of sandwich counter

parts.note: a filled roll is a kind of sandwich
a bar is a counter where drinks or food are served

explanation.surface: A sandwich bar's counter has some safety function.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll bar is the strong overhead frame protecting a car's occupants if it overturns.

clue.text: Negotiated reduction primarily available to similar dealers?

definitions.text: Negotiated reduction primarily available to similar dealers?

parts.words: Negotiated reduction primarily available to similar dealers?
parts.note: a price cut offered chiefly to buyers in the same line of business, read with a hint that negotiated means traded

explanation.surface: A bargained-for price cut is offered mainly to others in the same business.
explanation.walkthrough: Dealers in the same trade are 'similar dealers', and 'Negotiated' nods to TRADED, which runs into DISCOUNT at the start of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade discount is a reduction given by a supplier to retailers or others in the same business.

clue.text: Strange character shrouding centre of city

indicators.note: the letters kept are those wrapped round the middle of the city's name, its centre being removed

parts.note: London is the British capital

explanation.surface: An odd figure hides the heart of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the part of LONDON that shrouds its centre: lose the middle ND.
explanation.definitionFit: A loon is a crazy or eccentric person.

clue.text: Scoundrel is hoping to hide enjoyment

indicators.note: the words conceal the answer within their run of letters

explanation.surface: A villain hopes to keep his pleasure secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Relish is great pleasure or gusto, as in eating with relish.

clue.text: Criminal's caught out in scam

indicators.note: the letter for caught is taken out of the word

parts.note: a crook is a criminal; the 's reads as is
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A criminal is arrested while running a con.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught out' looks like being detected; it is C leaving CROOK.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to swindle or cheat them.

clue.text: Piece has essential parts for voice and choir introduced by speaker

indicators.note: the speaker's word comes first, leading in the rest

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker

indicators.note: the essential part of each word is its centre, so the middle letters are taken

explanation.surface: A composition requires the heart of voice and choir, presented by a narrator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word. The middle letters of voice and choir are I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large musical work for voices and orchestra, a musical piece.

clue.text: Ignore having no case to take on extra executive

indicators.note: the shortened word takes the extra letters into itself
the word ignore loses its casing, its first and last letters

parts.note: over means extra or surplus, as in left over

explanation.surface: A boss disregards a lawsuit's absence and takes on more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' suggests a lawsuit, but it is the casing of a word, its outer letters; 'having no case' strips them, and 'to take on' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor holds executive power, as in a state governor or prison governor.

clue.text: Conventional hot rod customised to break circuit times

indicators.note: the rearranged letters split the pair apart

parts.note: a circuit is round, like the letter O
the multiplication sign is X

indicators.note: a customised car is modified, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A traditional hot rod is modified to beat lap times at a racetrack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'customised' turns HOT ROD into RTHODO, which 'to break' puts between O and X.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthodox means following accepted, established norms.

clue.text: Material used to increase velocity of a pistol shot

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked, so the letters are broken up

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a powder that makes a bullet faster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' and 'velocity' suggest ballistics; it is canvas that drives a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A topsail is a sail set above the lowest one, cloth that drives a ship faster.

clue.text: Man disembowelled by fish is in grave state

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: serious and sombre

indicators.note: the shortened word stands by, next to, the fish

parts.note: sole is a flatfish

indicators.note: with its insides removed, only the first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: A man gutted by a fish is in a serious condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn means serious and dignified, without levity.

clue.text: Country's flag raised with backing of American head of state

definitions.note: read as country is, the noun before the link

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting a word up reads it upwards

parts.note: to flag is to tire

indicators.note: the pair of letters is read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, was Britain's queen and head of state

explanation.surface: A nation's banner is hoisted with American presidential support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner but is the verb; 'raised' reverses TIRE to ERIT and 'backing of' turns AER into REA.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a country in the Horn of Africa on the Red Sea.

clue.text: Reporter's crude language causes concern

indicators.note: what a reporter says is heard rather than read, so the sound counts

parts.note: pidgin is a simplified contact language

explanation.surface: A journalist's foul mouth causes worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude language' suggests swearing, but pidgin is a simplified language. 'causes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'not my pigeon' means not my business or responsibility.

clue.text: Valuing unexpected gift, he stops making money from scrap?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters plug the middle of the other word

parts.note: to prize something is to value it

indicators.note: the letters come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A man treasuring a surprise present gives up selling junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpected' turns GIFT HE into EFIGHT. 'scrap' looks like scrap metal but is a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Prizefighting is boxing for money, so a scrap, a fight, earns a purse.

clue.text: Fool may be unwelcome pain in the backside

definitions.meaning: to poke or pinch them on the bottom

explanation.surface: An idiot may be a real nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pain in the backside' looks like the idiom for a nuisance, but it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Goose names both a silly person and a prod in the rear.

clue.text: Brought up gossip about husband's sexual activity

indicators.note: the reversed word goes around the letter
in a down clue bringing a word up reads it upwards

parts.note: gas is idle chatter
H is short for husband; the 's is possessive

explanation.surface: Someone raised rumours of a husband's affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' reverses GAS to SAG, which goes 'about' H.
explanation.definitionFit: Shag is British slang for sexual intercourse.

clue.text: Cheer side short of team member after try

indicators.note: the number follows the word for try

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case
a football or cricket side has eleven players; one fewer leaves ten

explanation.surface: A rugby team with a player missing celebrates after scoring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' looks like rugby but is the legal sense; 'side' is eleven players, and one short is ten.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten someone is to encourage or cheer them up.

clue.text: Harlem bar got around Prohibition

indicators.note: the answer is found among these words, lying around within them

explanation.surface: A Harlem drinking den got around the alcohol ban of the 1920s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prohibition' suggests the US ban on alcohol, fitting the speakeasy picture, but it is any ban.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, especially on trade.

clue.text: Leader of gang completely fleeced victim

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
a fleeced sheep loses its coat, so the word loses its outside letters

parts.note: fully means completely

explanation.surface: A gang's boss has thoroughly swindled a sucker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleeced' looks like the definition (cheated) but strips FULLY to ULL.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull is a dupe, someone easily tricked.

clue.text: King gripped by novel about woman in service

indicators.note: the king's letter is held inside the reversed word
the word is turned about, read backwards

parts.note: novel means new
R is for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is captivated by a book about a female servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses NEW to WEN, which grips R. 'novel' looks like a book but means new.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wren was a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service, the British navy's women's branch.

clue.text: Stretch out punishment to overcome resistance

indicators.note: the letter goes over, inside, the punishment word

parts.note: the cane was a school punishment
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Extending a penalty to break down opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To crane is to stretch the neck out to see better.
